phone-bridge.name: Phone link
phone-bridge.description: Pair a phone by QR code to relay straight into the app (photos, scans, and more), over an optional Cloudflare tunnel.

phoneBridge.title: Phone link
phoneBridge.invalid: This link is no longer valid. Generate a new QR code on the desktop.

desktop.title: Scan with your phone
desktop.warmupNote: Waiting for the tunnel address to propagate so your phone can open it.
desktop.scanHint: Scan the code with the phone camera. It opens a MakeKeeper page tied to this window — whatever you scan or photograph on the phone arrives here.
desktop.linkHint: Can't scan it? Open this link on the phone.
desktop.localWarning: This is a local address — it won't open on your phone. Enable the tunnel in the plugin settings, or set PUBLIC_BASE_URL.
desktop.insecureWarning: This is an http:// address — the phone needs HTTPS. Enable the Cloudflare tunnel, or expose the app over HTTPS. If it is already served over HTTPS behind a reverse proxy, set PUBLIC_BASE_URL to the public https:// address (a proxy hop may have reset the forwarded scheme).

settings.intro:
Expose the app over HTTPS so a phone can pair with it. Uses an on-demand Cloudflare Quick Tunnel — no account or domain required.
Already served over HTTPS behind a reverse proxy? Set PUBLIC_BASE_URL to the public https:// address instead.

modeHints.off: No tunnel. Phone pairing works only if the app is already reachable over HTTPS.
modeHints.auto: A tunnel is started automatically when a session needs it, and stopped when idle.

settings.idleTtlLabel: Keep tunnel up after last use
settings.idleTtlHint: In Auto mode the tunnel stays up this long after the last session, then stops.

get_phone_bridge_status.description: Returns the state of public access for phone pairing: the Cloudflare tunnel mode (off/on/auto), the current state, the public URL (if up), and whether the cloudflared binary was found. Use it to tell whether a phone can currently reach the app over HTTPS.
